method: Daily closes. A bull is a Bitcoin cycle from its low to its high. A pullback is a drop of at least 15% that later closed back through its peak before that cycle high. The first 180 days after a coin's first bar are ignored. Each coin gets an equal vote. Shallow, typical, and deep are the 25th, 50th, and 75th percentiles of that vote. Worst is the deepest dip that still came back.

btc.reason: The early half of each bull was not clearly shallower than the late half, so the scale uses every resumed dip.

eth.reason: The early half was shallower than the late half (20% vs 27%), and the full set lands on that same typical depth. The scale uses every resumed dip.

alt.reason: The early half of each bull was not clearly shallower than the late half, so the scale uses every resumed dip.
